What does a CPU actually do?

Tech Compass · Updated 2026-10-19

IN THIS GUIDE

The quick answerAn everyday exampleCores and clock speedCPU or GPU?Further reading
THE QUICK ANSWER

The CPU executes the instructions that make software work. It handles calculations, decisions, and coordination across the computer.

An everyday example

When you open a spreadsheet, the CPU runs the program’s instructions and calculates formulas. The storage supplies the saved file, RAM holds active data, and graphics hardware helps display the result.

Cores and clock speed

A core can execute a stream of instructions. Multiple cores allow more work to happen at once when software can divide its tasks. Clock speed describes cycles per second, but architecture and workload matter too. A higher clock number alone does not prove one processor is faster.

CPU or GPU?

A CPU handles a broad range of tasks. A GPU is particularly suited to many similar calculations in parallel, such as drawing an image. They work together; one is not a universal replacement for the other.

What is a GPU?

A GPU is a processor designed to perform many calculations in parallel. It creates graphics for your screen and can also accelerate suitable computing tasks.

What is RAM?

RAM is your computer’s short-term working memory. It holds the information your apps are using right now. Storage keeps your files when the power is off; RAM does not.
